judged_text: The test "creates a topic view when a topic_id is found" verifies only that the TopicView mock was constructed with specific args ('TopicView.expects(:new).with(123, nil, {best: 5})') and never asserts anything about the rendered response body; the template then renders against a Mocha mock whose @topic_view.posts.present?, posts.each, and topic.url calls all return truthy mocks, so the 'success' assertion in the after block is satisfied by mock-driven garbage rendering. The test cannot distinguish a correctly rendered embed page from one that renders nothing meaningful: any regression in how @topic_view is consumed by app/views/embed/best.html.erb (e.g. best: 5 being ignored, posts not being passed through) passes as long as the constructor happens to be invoked with those arguments — the assertion verifies the mock call, not the behavior the test name promises.

adjudication.rationale: In `spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb`, the example `"creates a topic view when a topic_id is found"` only asserts `TopicView.new` is invoked with `(123, nil, {best: 5})` and does not validate any observable behavior (e.g., assigns, rendered body, or that posts are used). Also, this controller spec does not enable `render_views`, so it cannot catch regressions in `app/views/embed/best.html.erb` consumption of `@topic_view`. However, the finding’s claim that the template renders against a Mocha mock returning truthy values is not supported by the diff (no `render_views` and no return value configured).
